identity.title: Layer by Layer: Uncovering Hidden Representations in Language Models

problem.claim: The paper examines how representation quality varies across language-model layers and whether intermediate-layer features can outperform final-layer outputs.

gap.claim: It addresses the conventional view that earlier layers mainly capture low-level cues and that final layers are generally the appropriate source of representations.

contributions.claim: A unified framework of representation-quality metrics based on information theory, geometry, and invariance to input perturbations.
An analysis connecting layer-wise representation quality to the balance between information compression and signal preservation.
An evaluation of intermediate-layer representations across architectures, domains, and text-embedding tasks.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present a unified metric framework for explaining and quantifying hidden-layer properties, and use it to challenge the standard emphasis on final-layer embeddings.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report experiments on 32 text-embedding tasks spanning transformer and state-space architectures and language and vision domains.
They report that intermediate layers consistently provide stronger features across this evaluation and that mid-depth embeddings can exceed last-layer performance.
They report that intermediate layers often improve performance on a wide range of downstream tasks.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLM outputs typically rely on final layers because earlier layers are conventionally viewed as encoding low-level cues.
The analysis reports that intermediate layers can encode richer representations and often improve downstream performance.
The authors propose unified metrics grounded in information theory, geometry, and perturbation invariance to quantify hidden-layer properties.
The framework relates performance differences to each layer’s balance of information compression and signal preservation.
Experiments across 32 tasks, architectures, and domains report stronger intermediate-layer features and motivate further use of mid-layer representations.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a broad empirical claim about intermediate layers with a metric framework intended to explain it through compression, signal preservation, geometry, and invariance.

lessons.interpretation: A claim is more informative when its evaluation and proposed explanation are presented together.
lessons.application: When presenting a layer- or component-level finding, pair comparative evaluation with measurements tied to a stated explanatory mechanism.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the work is purely descriptive or when the proposed measurements have not been evaluated alongside the comparison.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify task-level results, baselines, numerical effect sizes, or statistical uncertainty.
It does not identify which layers, architectures, or domains show exceptions to the reported consistency.
The abstract does not provide details sufficient to assess metric validity, experimental reproducibility, or the scope of the claimed robustness and accuracy improvements.
